strategy_canvas.headline_thesis: Singapore SMEs can verify a counterparty's UEN and credit default, but no one captures peer-observed CONDUCT — late payment, bad-faith disputes, legal-threat bullying, phoenixing — keyed to UEN+directors, contestable and evidence-tied.

segments.name: Sub-contractors & M&E trades
segments.descriptor: Sub-cons and M&E specialists exposed to main-con non-payment, back-charges and pay-when-paid abuse.

segments.name: Wholesalers & distributors
segments.descriptor: Trade-credit-heavy distributors extending 30-90 day terms to a long tail of retailer/reseller buyers.

segments.name: F&B ingredient/equipment suppliers
segments.descriptor: Food, beverage and kitchen-equipment suppliers chasing thin-margin restaurant groups that churn and rebrand.

segments.name: Logistics & freight forwarders
segments.descriptor: Forwarders and 3PLs fronting disbursements, duties and haulage on credit for fast-moving SME shippers.

segments.name: Creative / IT / pro-services agencies
segments.descriptor: Agencies and consultancies exposed to scope-creep, ghosting, IP/NDA breach and milestone-withholding clients.

segments.name: SME finance & credit-control teams
segments.descriptor: In-house AR/credit teams setting terms and limits across hundreds of trade accounts.

segments.name: Invoice factoring & SME lenders
segments.descriptor: Factors, P2P platforms and lenders underwriting obligor and debtor risk before advancing against invoices.

segments.name: Corporate procurement / vendor onboarding
segments.descriptor: Procurement and KYB teams vetting new vendors for conduct, continuity and compliance before onboarding.

attack_plans.icp: SG M&E and specialist sub-contractors (10-80 staff) repeatedly burned by main-con late payment, back-charges and pay-when-paid stalling before signing the next package.
attack_plans.tam_estimate_sgd: S$9-14M/yr ARR ceiling: ~20,000 construction sub-con/M&E SMEs in SG, ~30% credit-pained and willing to pay ~S$40-60/mo or S$8/check at scale.
attack_plans.tam_reasoning: BCA registers tens of thousands of contractors; SOPA adjudication volume proves chronic payment conflict. Even 6,000 paying sub-cons at ~S$150/yr blended (subscription + checks) clears S$9M, before main-cons pay to manage their own reputation.
attack_plans.why_gap: ACRA shows a main-con's UEN and strike-off but never WHY or who it stiffed; SCCB lags and misses informal back-charges; the real signal lives in WhatsApp groups that are anonymous, undated and legally radioactive.
attack_plans.why_we_win: We bind every payment incident to the main-con's UEN+directors, date it, attach the retention/back-charge evidence, and let the main-con contest it — turning toxic chat gossip into a defensible, corroboration-weighted ledger no bureau can replicate.

gtm.channel: Trade associations (SCAL, SMECC), BCA contractor forums, and direct outreach to sub-con quantity surveyors and finance heads; seed with SOPA-adjudication public records.
gtm.pitch: Before you sign the next package, see how this main-con actually paid the last twenty sub-cons it hired — dated, evidenced, and contestable.
gtm.pricing: S$49/mo team plan with fair-use checks, or S$8 per one-off main-con lookup; first reputation report on your own UEN free to drive bidirectional sign-up.
gtm.content: A public 'Main-Con Payment Conduct Index' teaser, SOPA-case explainers, and a 'know before you bid' checklist gated behind UEN sign-in.

attack_plans.niche_name: Opacity Arbitrage: Glass-Box Conduct vs Black-Box Scores
attack_plans.icp: SME finance, AR and credit-control teams across distribution, F&B supply and logistics frustrated that bureau scores are opaque, un-actionable and unfair to disputing customers.
attack_plans.tam_estimate_sgd: S$12-18M/yr: ~280,000 active SG SMEs, a serviceable ~25,000 with a dedicated AR/credit function paying S$50-120/mo for a conduct layer alongside their bureau spend.
attack_plans.tam_reasoning: Credit teams already budget for Experian/SCCB; we sell a complementary, cheaper conduct lens, not a rip-and-replace. Capturing 10,000 teams at ~S$1,200/yr blended yields S$12M without displacing incumbent bureau contracts.
attack_plans.why_gap: Bureaus deliberately sell a number, not the incidents behind it; a credit manager can't show a disputing customer WHY their limit was cut, and the score reflects past default, not live slow-pay drift.
attack_plans.why_we_win: Every Lemon entry is an itemised, dated, evidence-tied incident the customer can contest — turning the bureau's opacity into our wedge: we are the glass box that sits next to their black box.

gtm.channel: Credit-management associations, AR-automation tool partnerships (integration listings), LinkedIn to AR/finance managers, and a comparison microsite.
gtm.pitch: Your bureau gives you a number you can't explain. We give you the dated, contestable incidents behind how a counterparty really behaves.
gtm.pricing: S$59/mo per team for a check allowance + monitoring; volume API tier for AR systems at per-call rates undercutting incumbent enterprise pricing.
gtm.content: A 'Why your credit score is a black box' explainer series, a free conduct-vs-default comparison tool, and PDPA-fair-dispute templates.

attack_plans.icp: Distributors, F&B suppliers and SME lenders repeatedly burned by directors who strike off a debt-laden shell and reopen under a fresh UEN owing the same creditors.
attack_plans.tam_estimate_sgd: S$6-10M/yr: phoenixing touches every credit-extending segment; a cross-segment monitoring product at S$30-80/mo to ~12,000 exposed SMEs underpins the range.
attack_plans.tam_reasoning: ACRA processes tens of thousands of strike-offs and winding-ups annually; a meaningful share are debt-shedding directors. A horizontal alert product priced low and sold across distribution, F&B and lending compounds into S$6M+ even at modest penetration.
attack_plans.why_gap: ACRA shows a UEN was struck off but not that the same directors relaunched, and never links the new entity to the creditors the old one burned; Handshakes maps the directors but carries no unpaid-debt trail.
attack_plans.why_we_win: We sit on top of ACRA strike-off data, link directors to their new and prior entities, and overlay the peer-logged unpaid-debt incidents — so a creditor gets an alert the moment a known bad-faith director re-emerges under a new UEN.

gtm.channel: ACRA open-data ingestion + alerting; distribution via trade associations, accounting/bookkeeping firms, and an embeddable 'phoenix alert' widget.
gtm.pitch: The director who didn't pay you last year just registered a new company. We tell you before you extend credit to the same person again.
gtm.pricing: S$29/mo watchlist with director-linked alerts; per-check S$8 for ad-hoc 'is this a phoenix?' lookups.
gtm.content: A monthly anonymised 'phoenix radar' digest, case studies of director-to-new-entity chains, and a free strike-off director lookup as a lead magnet.

attack_plans.niche_name: The KYB Conduct Layer for Vendor Onboarding
attack_plans.icp: Corporate procurement and vendor-onboarding teams that already run KYB (Sumsub/Handshakes) but have no behavioural-conduct signal to flag risky suppliers before approval.
attack_plans.tam_estimate_sgd: S$8-13M/yr: ~2,000-3,000 mid-to-large SG buyers running formal vendor onboarding, paying S$3-8k/yr for an API conduct layer plus per-check overage.
attack_plans.tam_reasoning: Procurement teams already pay for KYB and adverse-media; a conduct API is an incremental line item, not a new budget. Even 1,500 buyers at ~S$6k/yr blended (platform + API calls) reaches ~S$9M, with upside from supply-chain-continuity mandates.
attack_plans.why_gap: KYB tools verify a vendor IS who they say and map UBOs, but say nothing about how that vendor treats ITS sub-suppliers — the sub-tier non-payment and dispute conduct that drives real supply-chain-continuity risk.
attack_plans.why_we_win: We expose peer-observed conduct as a single API field that drops into existing onboarding flows, keyed to UEN+directors and contestable — the missing behavioural overlay on top of identity-only KYB.

gtm.channel: Direct enterprise sales to procurement and TPRM leads; integration partnerships with KYB/onboarding vendors and procurement platforms.
gtm.pitch: You verify a vendor exists. We tell you whether it pays its own suppliers and fights disputes in bad faith — before you onboard it.
gtm.pricing: Annual platform fee from S$3,000 + metered API calls; pilot at fixed price for a single high-risk vendor category.
gtm.content: A TPRM whitepaper on conduct vs identity risk, an API quickstart for onboarding teams, and a supply-chain-continuity scorecard demo.

attack_plans.icp: Industry and trade associations (construction, F&B supply, forwarders, agencies) whose members repeatedly warn each other about bad paymasters in legally exposed chat groups.
attack_plans.tam_estimate_sgd: S$4-7M/yr: dozens of SG trade bodies with member bases of hundreds to thousands; a white-labelled member-benefit watchlist at S$15-40k/yr per association plus member upsell.
attack_plans.tam_reasoning: Associations seek differentiated member benefits and already field 'is X a bad payer?' questions informally. Licensing a governed, PDPA-defensible watchlist to ~80 bodies at ~S$25k/yr blended, plus member subscriptions, supports the S$4-7M band.
attack_plans.why_gap: The conduct knowledge already exists inside association WhatsApp groups but is anonymous, undated, uncorroborated and a defamation liability the association itself can't endorse or formalise.
attack_plans.why_we_win: We convert that latent member knowledge into a corroboration-weighted, contestable, UEN-keyed watchlist the association can offer as a governed benefit — capturing a ready-made, trusted distribution channel and dense seed data in one move.

gtm.channel: Partnerships and revenue-share with trade associations; co-branded launch to their members; secretariat-led onboarding.
gtm.pitch: Turn your members' whispered warnings into a governed, fair, defensible counterparty watchlist — a benefit only your association can offer.
gtm.pricing: S$15-40k/yr white-label licence per association based on member count, with discounted member-tier subscriptions on top.
gtm.content: A member-benefit one-pager, a 'from chat group to defensible record' explainer, and an anonymised pilot watchlist for the launch association.

attack_plans.icp: Creative/IT/professional-services agencies and suppliers targeted by clients who weaponise spurious scope, quality or IP/NDA disputes and lawyer LODs to avoid final payment.
attack_plans.tam_estimate_sgd: S$5-8M/yr: ~30,000 SG agencies/consultancies and project-based suppliers; a serviceable ~15,000 acutely dispute-exposed paying ~S$30-50/mo or per-check.
attack_plans.tam_reasoning: Project-based vendors face concentrated final-milestone risk and remember every bad client. Converting 10,000 at ~S$500/yr blended (subscription + checks) reaches S$5M, with upside as the register extends into logistics and F&B dispute abuse.
attack_plans.why_gap: No incumbent captures litigious bad-faith conduct: bureaus score default, KYB verifies identity, adverse-media catches news — but the quiet pattern of a client manufacturing disputes to claw back fees is invisible until you're the next victim.
attack_plans.why_we_win: We register dated, evidence-tied legal-threat and bad-faith-dispute incidents keyed to UEN+directors, contestable by the accused — the only structured, defensible record of litigious conduct a vendor can check before signing.

gtm.channel: Agency and freelancer communities, professional-services bodies, contract-and-invoicing tool partnerships, and founder-network referral.
gtm.pitch: Some clients pay by manufacturing a dispute. Check the legal-threat register before you take the brief — dated, evidenced, contestable.
gtm.pricing: S$39/mo for agencies with a check allowance, or S$8 per client lookup; deposit-recommendation flag included.
gtm.content: A 'red flags of a non-paying client' guide, anonymised bad-faith-dispute pattern reports, and contract clause templates that pair with a pre-engagement check.
